causalLinks: each period's interest is the rate times the current balance
interest is added to the balance, so the next period's interest is computed on a bigger balance
more periods means more rounds of growth on growth
rubric.coreRule: Each period the balance is multiplied by (1 + rate), so after n periods it is principal times (1 + rate) to the power n.
rubric.whyRuleMatters: Because interest is earned on past interest, the balance grows by the same percentage each period, which means it grows by a bigger dollar amount every period.
rubric.whyRuleQuestion: Why does the dollar amount of interest get bigger each year even though the rate never changes?
rubric.anchorDescription: $100 at 2% interest, compounded once a year, is worth $110.41 after 5 years, not $110.
rubric.anchorPrompt: Where did the extra 41 cents come from, and what would it look like after 50 years?

contrastingCases.label: Simple interest
contrastingCases.detail: $100 at 2% simple interest earns $2 every year, always on the original $100. After 5 years: $110.00.
contrastingCases.oneLine: Interest only on the starting amount.

contrastingCases.label: Compound interest
contrastingCases.detail: $100 at 2% compounded yearly earns interest on the whole balance, including past interest. After 5 years: $110.41.
contrastingCases.oneLine: Interest on the balance, including past interest.

extremeCaseDimensions.description: The number of years gets very large.
Compounding happens every instant instead of once a year.

confusableNeighbors.label: Simple interest
confusableNeighbors.question: A loan charges $5 every year on a $100 balance, no matter what you owe. Compound or simple?
confusableNeighbors.correctDistinction: Simple interest is always computed on the original principal, so it grows by the same dollar amount each period (a straight line); compound interest is computed on the current balance, so it grows by the same percentage (a curve that bends up).

confusableNeighbors.label: Exponential decay
confusableNeighbors.question: A car loses 15% of its current value every year. Is that compound interest?
confusableNeighbors.correctDistinction: Same multiply-each-period structure, but the factor is below 1 (here 0.85), so the amount shrinks by a smaller dollar amount each period instead of growing by a bigger one.

transferStructuralRequirements: a quantity that changes each period
the change is a fixed percentage of the current amount, not of the starting amount
the new amount becomes the base for the next period
rubric.referenceTransferExample: A rumor where every person who knows it tells two new people each day: each day's new tellers are proportional to how many already know, so the count multiplies instead of adding.

misconceptions.label: Interest adds the same amount every year
misconceptions.tell: same amount each year, fixed dollar amount added, just add the interest times years, grows in a straight line
misconceptions.fix: That is simple interest. With compounding the percentage stays fixed but it applies to a bigger balance each year, so the dollar amount added grows.

misconceptions.label: Total growth is rate times years
misconceptions.tell: multiply rate by years, 2% for 5 years is 10%, double the time double the interest
misconceptions.fix: Rate times years ignores interest on interest. 2% for 5 years is 1.02 to the 5th, about 10.41%, and the gap widens with time.

misconceptions.label: Compounding more often makes money without limit
misconceptions.tell: compound more often infinite money, every second makes it huge, more compounding grows forever
misconceptions.fix: More frequent compounding helps less and less. $100 at 100% for a year: yearly gives $200, monthly $261.30, every instant $271.83 (100 times e). It levels off.

extremeCases.correctBehavior: Nothing grows: 1 + 0 is 1, and 1 to any power is 1, so the balance stays $100 for any number of years.
The balance reaches about $724.46, more than twice the $300 that simple interest gives, because the growth keeps building on itself.

extremeCases.scenario: $100 at 100% a year, compounded every instant, for one year.
extremeCases.correctBehavior: The balance tends to $100 times e, about $271.83, not infinity: splitting the year into more pieces gives smaller and smaller extra gains.
